investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict. The scheduler message is identical across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable nodes for scheduling.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules, so no node can accept a new remote-agent pod. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 137s before the eval timed out.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message (146s stuck, latencyMs=152689), confirming the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message (144s stuck, latencyMs=146296), confirming all three remote-agent checks hit the same scheduler rejection.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}); no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written because the pod never started.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent could return.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled, no VM ID or state is ever returned to populate evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141188 (~141s); warningLatencyMs=240000 and outageLatencyMs=360000 per source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183 — the check failed well within the outage threshold, meaning the scheduler rejection, not a timeout, drove the failure.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots on the only two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, which may indicate a cluster topology change (e.g., node labels removed or nodes replaced) that reduced the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding VM slots: a prior eval run or user workload may have left pods running that are consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota without being cleaned up, preventing new scheduling.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote-agent pods than is now required, and no autoscaling or node-pool expansion has been triggered.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the Insufficient message would indicate a scheduler bug or label mismatch rather than true capacity exhaustion.

If all 6 nodes are found to satisfy the pod's node affinity rules, the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would indicate a dynamic label change or node replacement that occurred between the pod spec being written and the eval running.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing one VM slot succeeds and produces all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), that would confirm capacity exhaustion as the sole cause.
If the eval passes without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent pod creation that has since resolved) rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all nodes and warns before the pool is fully exhausted, providing earlier signal than waiting for a pod to be rejected.
Add a node-affinity coverage check that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's selector rules, alerting if the eligible node pool drops below a safe threshold.
Add a zombie-pod detection eval that lists pods requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm older than a configurable TTL and flags them as leaked resources.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the raw Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence key (e.g., schedulerMessage) so future failures include the rejection reason directly in the evidence object rather than only in the check message string.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can poll state, the pod scheduling failure prevented agent creation entirely, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. At the time of the eval run, 0/6 nodes were available: the 2 affinity-matching nodes both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). The pod remained unscheduled for ~137–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, which is why no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

This is directly stated in all three scheduler messages (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict. The scheduler message is identical across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable nodes for scheduling.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules, so no node can accept a new remote-agent pod. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 137s before the eval timed out.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message (146s stuck, latencyMs=152689), confirming the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message (144s stuck, latencyMs=146296), confirming all three remote-agent checks hit the same scheduler rejection.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}); no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written because the pod never started.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent could return.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled, no VM ID or state is ever returned to populate evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141188 (~141s); warningLatencyMs=240000 and outageLatencyMs=360000 per source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183 — the check failed well within the outage threshold, meaning the scheduler rejection, not a timeout, drove the failure.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots on the only two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, which may indicate a cluster topology change (e.g., node labels removed or nodes replaced) that reduced the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding VM slots: a prior eval run or user workload may have left pods running that are consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota without being cleaned up, preventing new scheduling.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote-agent pods than is now required, and no autoscaling or node-pool expansion has been triggered.

followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all nodes and warns before the pool is fully exhausted, providing earlier signal than waiting for a pod to be rejected.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the raw Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence key (e.g., schedulerMessage) so future failures include the rejection reason directly in the evidence object rather than only in the check message string.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was intentionally set to target only 2 nodes and those nodes had available VM slots would shift the diagnosis toward a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a taint, resource quota, or admission policy) rather than capacity exhaustion.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime at the same timestamp would indicate the failure is isolated to the remote-agent-state probe path rather than a shared infrastructure constraint.
Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes previously matched the pod's affinity/selector would indicate a node label regression as the primary cause rather than VM slot exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on affinity-eligible nodes and fails with a warning before full exhaustion is reached.

Add a pre-flight scheduling dryrun eval that submits a test pod with the same node affinity/selector and resource requests as remote-agent pods and verifies it would be schedulable before attempting full agent creation.

Add an eval that counts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector and alerts if the count drops below a configured minimum (e.g., below 2), catching node label drift early.

Add a pod-leak detection eval that counts long-running kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods in the remote-agents namespace and alerts if any exceed a maximum expected lifetime, preventing slot exhaustion from leaked eval artifacts.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed between 09:16 and 09:21 UTC on 2026-06-19 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during this eval window timed out (~137–152 s) without ever starting, producing zero evidence output and a hard eval failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is confirmed only at the eval level.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918 (line 1918): 'const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)' — agent creation is the first blocking async call; a scheduling failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189 (line 185): remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000, confirming this check is non-required but still tracked for feature health.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM slots are fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. All three sibling checks report the same constraint (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 nodes that do not match the pod's affinity rules may have had labels removed, taints added, or selector criteria tightened, shrinking the schedulable node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes. This would compound the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote-agent pods from a prior eval run consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and not releasing them, preventing new scheduling. The eval runner uses withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods holding VM slots.

reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the nodes that match the remote-agent pod's affinity selector and check the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource allocatable vs. requested values.

reproductionSteps.details: Identify whether any remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are stuck in a non-terminal state and consuming VM slots that should have been released by withCleanup().

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks fail with the same Kubernetes Unschedulable event citing kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion. The failure occurs before any application code runs. Evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state.

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the 2 affinity-eligible cluster nodes
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on exactly 2 nodes, which are the only nodes satisfying the pod's affinity selector. This is the binding constraint.

affectedAreas.label: Node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by affinity rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes. If affinity rules have drifted or node labels changed, the eligible pool may have shrunk.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs
affectedAreas.reason: The probe at line 1918 calls createAgent() which triggers pod scheduling. A scheduling failure here prevents all evidence collection, causing the full contract gap (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

affectedAreas.label: withCleanup() pod lifecycle management in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs
affectedAreas.reason: If prior eval runs left orphaned pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots due to incomplete cleanup, those slots would not be available for new scheduling attempts.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod affinity selector to determine whether the resource pool is at ceiling.

Audit the production namespace for orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots; terminate any non-terminal pods that should have been cleaned up by withCleanup() in run-status-probes.mjs.
Review the node affinity/selector rules applied to remote-agent pods and compare against current node labels on all 6 cluster nodes to determine whether the eligible pool has shrunk unexpectedly.

If the VM pool is genuinely at capacity due to legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the 2 eligible nodes can be increased or whether additional eligible nodes can be added to the affinity pool.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any remediation to confirm all 5 required evidence fields are returned and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (features.json line 185), but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183–184); prioritize restoring scheduling capacity for the required checks first.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is still present or has self-resolved. A pass would return all 5 required evidence fields and a message containing 'hello from aura' per the contract at check-expectations.json line 268–269.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the resource exhaustion hypothesis without running a full eval.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe nodes with a selector matching the remote-agent pod affinity to read the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used counts.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List non-terminal remote-agent pods in the production namespace via kubectl
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether orphaned pods from prior eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get pods -n <production-namespace> with a label selector for remote-agent pods and filter for non-Completed, non-Failed states.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Verify node affinity label consistency across all 6 cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out or confirms the node affinity misconfiguration hypothesis.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get nodes --show-labels and compare against the affinity selector used by remote-agent pods to confirm whether the 4/2 split is expected or represents label drift.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared constraint
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the constraint is definitively at the cluster scheduler level and not isolated to the runtime probe logic.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduler constraint must be investigated.

If a fresh eval run immediately after this report succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the condition was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released VM slots) rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.
If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity rules are shown to have always been excluded (i.e., affinity configuration has not changed), then node affinity drift is not a contributing factor.
If no orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods are found in the production namespace, the leaked-pod hypothesis is disproved and the cause is purely capacity ceiling or a workload spike.

If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) are also failing at the same time, the failure scope may be broader than the remote-agent VM pool and a different shared dependency should be investigated.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that counts non-terminal remote-agent pods in the production namespace after each eval run to detect cleanup failures in withCleanup() before they accumulate and exhaust VM slots.
Add a node-affinity-health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod affinity selector, alerting if the eligible pool drops below a configured minimum.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes scheduling timeouts (pod never started) from runtime failures (pod started but returned wrong output), to make triage faster when the Unschedulable condition recurs.
